reply.thought: Before recording any payout, I need to confirm the refunds table contains every requested refund at the requested amount, so I'll read it first.
The refunds table contains all three requested refunds at the requested amounts, so the pre-payout check passes. Next I need the customer list from the orders.

The refunds table matches all three requested refunds at the requested amounts, so the pre-payout check passes. The orders list shows three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance before recording payouts.
Acme's net balance is 7125 cents. The refunds check passed, so I'll get birch's net balance next.
Acme's balance is 7125 and birch's is 55306. Cobalt is the last customer in the orders list, so I need its net balance before recording any payouts.
The refunds check passed, and each balance matches orders minus refunds (acme 28768-21643=7125, birch 55306, cobalt 39255-10428=28827). I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout of 7125 is recorded. Birch's net balance is 55306, which matches its orders (36544 + 18762) with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 28827 matches its orders (18183 + 21072 = 39255) minus its refund (10428). All three customers are now verified, so I'll record cobalt's payout.
All three payouts recorded successfully. Each balance matches orders minus refunds, and the refunds table matched the requested refunds before any payout was recorded.
